speaker: The Heroine
text: Hi.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Welcome to LAiDIES.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Before the season starts, I owe you a tour.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is a show about learning AI — made for women who are already smart, already busy, and not remotely interested in a forty-hour course.

speaker: The Heroine
text: It works like the TV we grew up on: twenty-four episode seasons, a new one every Wednesday.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Each episode is shorter than your commute, and each one gives you exactly one useful thing — explained the way your sharpest girlfriend would explain it over coffee, with the pop culture you were raised on and none of the jargon you weren't.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I'm your heroine.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I can't say that with a straight face either, but the promo guy insists.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I'm not an expert — I'm a few steps ahead of you, that's all.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I put off learning AI for longer than I'll admit on the record — the full confession is Episode One — and now I'm walking the road one Wednesday at a time and reporting back.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I make the mistakes so you can skip them.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I do the reading so you don't have to.

speaker: The Heroine
text: So what can you expect in season one?

speaker: The Heroine
text: Remember the promo guy?

speaker: The Heroine
text: He's been pacing the booth, dying to do his big voice.

speaker: The Heroine
text: So I'll let him set up the season, and I'll meet you on the other side for the actual tour.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Take it away.

speaker: The Announcer
text: On this season of LAiDIES: she stops feeling behind.

speaker: The Announcer
text: She learns to delegate to machines — without lowering her standards.

speaker: The Announcer
text: She builds her own little squad of AI helpers.

speaker: The Announcer
text: And she becomes the woman other people come to when the future gets confusing.

speaker: The Announcer
text: But first... the tour.

speaker: The Announcer
text: This is the trailer: Welcome to SUNNYVAiLE.

speaker: The Heroine
text: So — SUNNYVAiLE.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The 90s had Sunnydale, Bayside, and Capeside.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Silicon Valley has SUNNYVAiLE.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You have sunnyVEIL.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Thats Sunny v-A-I-l-e.

speaker: The Heroine
text: See what we did there?

speaker: The Heroine
text: When I finally started learning this stuff, everything about AI looked like a stock photo of a glowing blue brain.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And I refused to spend a year of Wednesdays somewhere that ugly.

speaker: The Heroine
text: So we built a town instead — set somewhere around nineteen ninety-nine, and furnished with the entire era that raised us.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Call it nineteen ninety to twenty ten.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Boy bands and girl groups.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Sleepover games.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Hair full of butterfly clips.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Calling in to the radio station to request a song so you could record it on cassette.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The glory days of twenty-four-episode seasons, back when they let you fall in love with the characters before cancelling everything.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That era wired us — and it turns out it wired us perfectly for this.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Because SUNNYVAiLE is where Girl power meets machine power.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Analogies that stick.

speaker: The Heroine
text: In a fictional town from an era we know and love.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That's how we're teaching it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Ladies is the show, SUNNYVAiLE is where every episode takes place.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And I live here — actually live here.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I found this place at eleven p.m. on a Tuesday, looking for something else.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Most residents do.

speaker: The Heroine
text: My card's in my wallet, my closet's upstairs at the sorority house, and the story you'll hear this season happens in these streets: the late-night research at the library, the coffee at my corner table, the songs on the radio.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Every building is a page.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Walking in is just clicking.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And the town remembers your visits — hold that thought.

speaker: The Heroine
text: But here's what I actually need you to hear, because at first glance it looks like we just built something cute.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The town IS the teaching method.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Every episode teaches one concept.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The study pack reinforces it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The song turns it into an earworm you can't shake.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The pop quiz tests it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The games make you practice it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The community pressure-checks it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Every part of town echoes every other part, on purpose — because when you're busy, that echo is what makes learning stick.

speaker: The Heroine
text: We think in analogies and stories; that's not a weakness, it's how AI finally makes sense.

speaker: The Heroine
text: We built a world because worlds work.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And one more thing before the walking starts — I keep saying Wednesday...because on wednesdays we do AI (obviously), but let me tell you what Wednesday actually means.

speaker: The Heroine
text: A new episode drops every Wednesday, and the town dresses for it: new anthem on the radio, new study pack at the coffee shop, new charms hidden around town...(we might even wear pink!) But the town itself is open every day of the week, and nothing expires.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You can visit any building and do any activity in any order, on its own, whenever you want.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Start today.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Start next month.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Go back to episode one — the tapes stay on the shelf at the rental store forever — catch up at your own pace, binge a little if you're behind, or slow down and sit with one.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Come back anytime for a re-read, a re-watch, a re-listen, or to have have fun with one activities.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Wednesday is when the new thing arrives.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Every other day is yours.

speaker: The Heroine
text: But if you want to get the most out of SUNNYVAiLE, do one of the weekly tours so the learning really sticks.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You might even meet some new friends along the way.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Now.

speaker: The Heroine
text: There are two types of tours in SUNNYVAiLE and both count.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The Express Tour is four stops: the week's episode; the study pack, the quiz, and the song.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The Full Tour is the loop — eight stops through town, all tracked by your Tour Guide who ticks each stop automatically the moment you show up.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Finish all eight before next Wednesday and you bank an extra wish with the Fairy Godmother.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I'll introduce her in a minute.

speaker: The Heroine
text: It's the nineties.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Just go with it.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Here's the Full Tour, in walking order.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop one: the NewsStand — first door on Main Street.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The week's AI headlines, translated into actual English: what happened, why it matters to your job, no doom, no hype.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Plus the bigger themes we are tracking in AI.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Five minutes, and you're the informed one in the meeting.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop two: the Chick Flicks, our video rental store.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Every episode lives here like a tape on a shelf, sorted into genre aisles you can actually browse.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Grab this week's — and if you want the full experience, there's a screening room in the back where episodes play with the pictures — the premiere is screening now.

speaker: The Heroine
text: It's where you'd take a friend for her first one.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop three: the Blend and Snap — the coffee shop, and third on the loop because by now you'll want to sit down.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is where the week's study pack lives: the class notes — a cheat sheet of what the episode taught and what to remember for the quiz — plus this week's trading card pack.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Rip it open, flip each card, learn a concept.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Old packs stay on the back shelf, so you can always catch up.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I write half this show from the corner table.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The pack also hands you the try-on: each week's ten-minute exercise, where you try the lesson on one small, real task from your actual life.

speaker: The Heroine
text: If you only do one thing beyond listening, do the try-on.

speaker: The Heroine
text: It's why the pack exists.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop four: SUNNYVAiLE High, up Schoolhouse Road.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The pop quiz — ten questions on the episode, plus 2 bonus questions, a couple of minutes, and your score banks butterfly clips in a jar in your closet.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Best score counts, so you can always retake.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And every four weeks, the gym hosts a book fair.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Yes, that kind.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Yes, with posters.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop five is scheduled free time — my favourite kind of structure.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is when the town shows off.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Get your cards read at Madame Cleo's; she does walk-ins, and she will tell you the read, the message, and the move.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Her fortunes do NOT disappoint!

speaker: The Heroine
text: I go more often than I'm prepared to admit.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Pick up the Dream Phone and call somebody in nineteen ninety-nine.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Ask the Fairy Godmother anything — she's the town's actual AI assistant, a real one: bring the question, she brings the answer.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And yes, that wish you banked for finishing the Full Tour?

speaker: The Heroine
text: Spent with her.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Or go hunting: every week, seven charms hide in pictures around town.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Spot one, click it, and it's added to your charm bracelet in your closet.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop six: Makeover on Main.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is where you get your SUNNYVAiLE glow up.... your residence card.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The town's version of a membership, and the two most useful minutes on the tour.

speaker: The Heroine
text: It's free.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You pick a handle, and from then on the town remembers you: quiz clips, charms, stickers, wishes, tour progress — everything banks.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Without a card you're a tourist; things happen, but nothing sticks.

speaker: The Heroine
text: With one, you're a resident.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And you can come back any week to freshen the card after you've completed the week— your favourite saint, your favourite cocktail, your favourite quote.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Stop seven: the Bronze Age.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Happy hour.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The bar serves the Businesswomen's Special — a paper fortune teller, the kind you folded in fifth grade, picks your drink of the week.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is your reminder to book that overdue happy hour with the girls— and we even have tools to help make scheduling and meeting easy and fun.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And stop eight: the sorority house — Delta Lai Nu, on Wisteria Lane.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The rooms live here — our members-only chat, a full hallway of them in three wings.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Common rooms, where you post your wins and we cheer, or ask the house anything.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Advice rooms, like Dear Ladies.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Creative rooms, where mix CDs get traded and the Burn Book collects what didn't work — we keep receipts on our own mistakes.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And the feature of the house: Girl Talk, where you draw a card and take the dare.

speaker: The Heroine
text: This is also where the weekly sign-off challenge lands.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And upstairs?

speaker: The Heroine
text: Your closet — the room where everything you've collected is on display.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Your card.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Your clips.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Your charms.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Your luminaries.

speaker: The Heroine
text: End the loop there, and admire the shelf you're building.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Now — the radio.

speaker: The Heroine
text: I saved it because it's my favourite building in town, and because it is not just where the episode songs live.

speaker: The Heroine
text: K-S-V-L, community radio, ninety-nine point nine, at the end of Main Street — a full, functioning station.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Turn on the live rotation and you get DJ SunnyV between tracks, station jingles, weather and traffic reports for a town that has neither weather nor traffic, and commercials for the storefronts you just walked past.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The music is real and it's ours: ten house bands — every name is an AI joke you'll start catching around episode six — plus a new anthem every episode, because every lesson here has its own song.

speaker: The Heroine
text: There are mix CDs you can flip over and read like it's your best friend's handwriting.

speaker: The Heroine
text: There's a sticker rack, and your first one's free.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The station has one belief, and honestly it's the town's pedagogy in six words: don't just learn from books.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Learn from hooks.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Turn it on when you arrive — it follows you from building to building.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And there's still more I'm leaving for you to find.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The post office writes you one letter a week — the episode, the pack, the quiz, the news, and the song, all in one envelope — and it ships gifts too: send a note, a charm, or a saint card to a friend in town.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The mall sells flair for your card.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Town Hall is run by Mayor Deb — and Deb deserves a proper introduction.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Deb worked at the post office until nineteen ninety-nine, when her coworkers put her name on the mayoral ballot as a joke.

speaker: The Heroine
text: She won.

speaker: The Heroine
text: She keeps winning.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Nobody is more surprised than Deb, who also happens to be our Patron Saint of Loop Me Out.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Her campaign posters alone are worth the trip to Town Hall.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And up on Lantern Hill, the Luminairy hangs portraits of the women (and one rose) in three wings: the patron saints from the era that raised us, teaching us the lessons of today, the real-life mavens who built and questioned this field, and the trailblazers shipping the frontier right now.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Take the walk.

speaker: The Heroine
text: The town rewards snooping.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You'll have favourites by Friday.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Everything I just described lives at laidies.ai.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That's "LAiDIES" spelled with an i in the middle: L, A, i, D, I, E, S.

speaker: The Heroine
text: New episode every Wednesday.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Express when you're slammed, Full Tour when you've got the hour, any day of the week that works for you.

speaker: The Heroine
text: Do it all at once, or one stop at a time.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That's the town.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That's the show.

speaker: The Heroine
text: That's the deal.

speaker: The Heroine
text: So remember, LAiDIES: you don't have to know anything yet.

speaker: The Heroine
text: You just have to show up.

speaker: The Heroine
text: See you next Wednesday... in SUNNYVAiLE.

speaker: The Heroine
text: And now back to our promo guy...

speaker: The Announcer
text: And on the next episode of LAiDIES: a man named Steve is called a visionary... and our heroine finally stops putting it off.

speaker: The Announcer
text: Tune in next week for Episode One: On Wednesdays We Use AI.
